raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On a pinned-tactic DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash baseline, small-batch WQKV-A and shared
FC1 launch only 14 and 9 CTAs per layer on B300. FlashInfer's existing
cluster-local split-K=4 improves their kernel latency. A target-only serving
A/B measured a 1.25% plain decode-throughput improvement and a 1.00% reduction
in mean full-request latency.

**Draft:** those serving measurements used SGLang
`bf9a666c7495e85f651849f154cffd0f94adb39d`, not the latest main. Current main
autotunes small-M MXFP8 calls and may already choose split-K. This PR enables
the narrowly scoped policy by default, with an explicit opt-out. A speedup
over current main has not been measured.

## Modifications

- Enable `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_SMALL_BATCH_SPLIT_K` by default; set it to `0`
  to disable the policy.
- Apply only to the target model's `self_attn.wqkv_a` and
  `mlp.shared_experts.gate_up_proj`. NextN/DSPARK draft constructors do not
  install the override.
- Use split-K=4 only on B300/SM103, CuTe DSL, BF16 output, M=1..8 and local
  (N,K)=(1792,5120) or (1152,5120), with contiguous swizzled MXFP8 operands.
  Other calls retain their existing dispatch.
- Preserve the existing path under deterministic inference or batch-invariant
  mode. The selected tactic bypasses autotuning only for eligible calls.
- Reuse the existing linear dispatch and custom-op/fake-op boundary, plus
  FlashInfer's CuTe runner and input validation. There is no process-wide
  runner monkey patch or new CUDA kernel.
- Add GPU tests, including default-enabled and explicit opt-out behavior.

The explicit tactic currently needs FlashInfer's private runner API because
public `mm_mxfp8` has no tactic argument. This dependency is isolated in the
existing MXFP8 custom-op wrapper and needs review before promotion from draft.

## Accuracy Tests

The PR's GPU tests cover both shapes at M=1/2/4/6/8 against an independent FP32
GEMM of dequantized operands (relative L2 < 0.5%), prequantized-input parity,
unsupported shape/dtype/hardware fallbacks, both consistency controls,
model default and opt-out wiring, bias/leading dimensions, CUDA Graph replay
with changed inputs, scale length/dtype validation, and the torch.compile
custom-op boundary.

Validation completed on B300 with the PR source and FlashInfer 0.7.2:
`python test/registered/kernels/ops/gemm/test_dsv41_mxfp8_split_k.py`
passed all six tests with warmed compilation caches. The environment
used PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130; the complete current-main PyTorch 2.14.1 environment
and full-model serving were not tested. The initial five cases also passed
with FlashInfer 0.6.18 before the additional scale-buffer regression case.
All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including registered-test validation.

The prior 60-case isolated sweep had relative L2 error < 1% against FP32 and
maximum relative L2 difference 4.71e-5 against the original BF16 outputs.
Split-K changes reduction order and is not bitwise equivalent. Checkpoint-level
accuracy/model-quality parity has not been established.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Historical serving A/B: four B300 GPUs, TP4/EP4, FlashInfer 0.6.18,
PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130; twelve natural SPEED-Bench prompts, mean input 1074 tokens,
two repetitions/configuration, concurrency 1, 512 greedy output tokens.
All 96 requests completed. Cache was flushed before requests; profiling was
separate from timing.

| Metric | Baseline | Split-K=4 | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Plain median TPOT | 3.58360 ms | 3.53936 ms | -1.23% |
| Plain decode throughput | 279.05 tok/s | 282.54 tok/s | +1.25% |
| Plain mean request latency | 2069.83 ms | 2049.14 ms | -1.00% |
| DSPARK mean request latency | 1144.46 ms | 1132.45 ms | -1.05%, inconclusive |
| DSPARK weighted acceptance length | 2.90634 | 2.93200 | +0.88% |

Plain trial median TPOT was 3.58422/3.58306 -> 3.53848/3.54034 ms.
DSPARK's paired prompt-bootstrap 95% interval includes zero (-2.52% to +4.58%).
Its pooled median TPOT change of -6.73% is acceptance-sensitive and is not
presented as a reproducible kernel gain. Sequential runs do not exclude drift.

Separate serving traces measured WQKV 7.390 -> 5.842 us/call and shared FC1
6.974 -> 5.110 us/call. Shared-expert work largely overlaps routed experts,
which explains why additive kernel savings exceed end-to-end savings. Every
eligible optimized target graph contained exactly 40+40 split-K calls;
baseline and draft graphs contained none. There was no separate projection
ablation or high-concurrency measurement.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add focused GPU tests with CI registration.
- [x] Include measured results and limitations in the PR description.
- [ ] Establish checkpoint-level accuracy and current-main serving performance.
- [x] Keep the policy scoped and provide an explicit opt-out.

+"""B300 dense split-K: numerical accuracy, fallbacks and graph replay."""
+
+import unittest
+from functools import partial
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.quantization import fp8_utils
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_exec
+from sglang.srt.utils import get_device_sm
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase, published_topology
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=60, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="2-gpu-gb300")
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(get_device_sm() == 103, "B300 small-batch MXFP8 policy")
+class TestDsv41Mxfp8SplitK(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        super().setUp()
+        self.enterContext(published_topology())
+        torch.manual_seed(42)
+
+    def _operands(self, m=6, n=1792, k=5120):
+        from flashinfer import mxfp8_quantize
+
+        x = torch.randn(m, k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        w = torch.randn(n, k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.02
+        wq, ws = mxfp8_quantize(w, is_sf_swizzled_layout=True, alignment=32)
+        return x, w, wq, ws
+
+    def _reference(self, x, w):
+        from flashinfer import SfLayout, mxfp8_quantize
+
+        def dequantize(t):
+            q, s = mxfp8_quantize(
+                t,
+                is_sf_swizzled_layout=False,
+                alignment=32,
+                sf_swizzle_layout=SfLayout.layout_linear,
+            )
+            scale = torch.exp2(s.view(t.shape[0], -1).float() - 127)
+            return q.float() * scale.repeat_interleave(32, dim=1)
+
+        previous_tf32 = torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32
+        torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False
+        try:
+            return dequantize(x) @ dequantize(w).t()
+        finally:
+            torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = previous_tf32
+
+    def _linear(self, x, wq, ws, **kwargs):
+        return fp8_utils.flashinfer_mxfp8_blockscaled_linear(
+            x, wq, ws, backend="cute-dsl", pin_tactic=True, **kwargs
+        )
+
+    @torch.inference_mode()
+    def test_numerics_and_prequantized_input(self):
+        """Check the split reduction against an independent dequantized GEMM."""
+        from flashinfer import mxfp8_quantize
+
+        for n in (1792, 1152):
+            for m in (1, 2, 4, 6, 8):
+                with self.subTest(m=m, n=n):
+                    x, w, wq, ws = self._operands(m=m, n=n)
+                    reference = self._reference(x, w)
+                    with patch.object(
+                        fp8_utils,
+                        "flashinfer_mm_mxfp8",
+                        wraps=fp8_utils.flashinfer_mm_mxfp8,
+                    ) as gemm:
+                        actual = self._linear(x, wq, ws, use_small_batch_split_k=True)
+                    self.assertTrue(gemm.call_args.kwargs["use_split_k"])
+                    self.assertTrue(torch.isfinite(actual).all())
+                    error = torch.linalg.vector_norm(actual.float() - reference)
+                    self.assertLess(
+                        (error / torch.linalg.vector_norm(reference)).item(), 0.005
+                    )
+                    q, sf = mxfp8_quantize(x, is_sf_swizzled_layout=True, alignment=32)
+                    prequantized = self._linear(
+                        q, wq, ws, input_scale=sf, use_small_batch_split_k=True
+                    )
+                    torch.testing.assert_close(prequantized, actual, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+    @torch.inference_mode()
+    def test_default_and_unsupported_cases_preserve_output(self):
+        """The policy cannot change other M/N/K shapes, dtypes or hardware."""
+        for m, n, k, dtype in (
+            (9, 1792, 5120, torch.bfloat16),
+            (1, 128, 5120, torch.bfloat16),
+            (1, 1792, 2560, torch.bfloat16),
+            (1, 1792, 5120, torch.float16),
+        ):
+            with self.subTest(m=m, n=n, k=k, dtype=dtype):
+                x, _, wq, ws = self._operands(m=m, n=n, k=k)
+                x = x.to(dtype)
+                expected = self._linear(x, wq, ws)
+                with patch.object(
+                    fp8_utils,
+                    "flashinfer_mm_mxfp8",
+                    wraps=fp8_utils.flashinfer_mm_mxfp8,
+                ) as gemm:
+                    actual = self._linear(x, wq, ws, use_small_batch_split_k=True)
+                self.assertFalse(gemm.call_args.kwargs.get("use_split_k", False))
+                torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+        x, _, wq, ws = self._operands()
+        expected = self._linear(x, wq, ws)
+        with patch.object(fp8_utils, "get_device_sm", return_value=100):
+            actual = self._linear(x, wq, ws, use_small_batch_split_k=True)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+    @torch.inference_mode()
+    def test_deterministic_and_batch_invariant_bypass(self):
+        """Both consistency controls must retain the original reduction."""
+        from sglang.srt.batch_invariant_ops import (
+            disable_batch_invariant_mode,
+            enable_batch_invariant_mode,
+        )
+
+        x, _, wq, ws = self._operands()
+        expected = self._linear(x, wq, ws)
+        with (
+            get_exec().deterministic.override(enable_deterministic_inference=True),
+            patch.object(
+                fp8_utils, "flashinfer_mm_mxfp8", wraps=fp8_utils.flashinfer_mm_mxfp8
+            ) as gemm,
+        ):
+            actual = self._linear(x, wq, ws, use_small_batch_split_k=True)
+        self.assertFalse(gemm.call_args.kwargs.get("use_split_k", False))
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        enable_batch_invariant_mode()
+        try:
+            with patch.object(
+                fp8_utils, "flashinfer_mm_mxfp8", wraps=fp8_utils.flashinfer_mm_mxfp8
+            ) as gemm:
+                actual = self._linear(x, wq, ws, use_small_batch_split_k=True)
+            self.assertFalse(gemm.call_args.kwargs.get("use_split_k", False))
+            torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        finally:
+            disable_batch_invariant_mode()
+
+    @torch.inference_mode()

+    @torch.inference_mode()
+    def test_graph_replay_bias_and_leading_dimensions(self):
+        """Replay must consume changed inputs and preserve bias/output shaping."""
+        x, _, wq, ws = self._operands()
+        x = x.view(2, 3, 5120)
+        bias = torch.randn(1792, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        call = partial(
+            self._linear, wq=wq, ws=ws, bias=bias, use_small_batch_split_k=True
+        )
+        call(x)
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+            actual = call(x)
+        for amplitude in (0, 0.1, 3):
+            x.normal_().mul_(amplitude)
+            graph.replay()
+            expected = call(x)
+            self.assertEqual(actual.shape, (2, 3, 1792))
+            torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        compiled = torch.compile(call, backend="eager", fullgraph=True)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(compiled(x), expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
